processing: Darjeeling orthodox black tea made as specialty lots for international sale.
harvest_season: Picking starts after winter dormancy, around February; as elsewhere in Darjeeling, first and second flush are the prized pickings.
appearance_dry: As is typical of Darjeeling, twisted leaf in a mix of green, silver and brown tones.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold to amber by flush, as is typical of Darjeeling.
taste_profile: Sold as an organic specialty Darjeeling; little is recorded about the taste of this garden itself, and it is reasonable to expect the usual floral spring and fruitier summer character.

brewing.notes: Western-style. Treat a spring lot gently; a pale liquor is no reason to steep longer.

vintage_note: Sold under the garden name by year and flush, as is usual for Darjeeling, and bought for freshness. Drink within a year or two. Spring lots appear first and tend to cost the most.
description:
Arya is a small specialty garden in the Darjeeling Sadar subdivision, sitting at about 1,500 metres. It is one of those names that Darjeeling drinkers recognise on the label, and sellers offer it as organic.

The tea is made as specialty lots for export, not for the mass market. Beyond that, little is documented about how its methods differ from those of its neighbours.

As with other Darjeelings, go gently with spring teas and allow summer lots more time. Taste at two and a half minutes first.

The road up is famously steep, a fact more amusing than useful when buying. What matters is the year and the flush on the packet.
history:
The estate was established in 1885 and first went by the name Sidrabong. Legend has it that Buddhist monks founded the garden and raised varieties from Chinese seed, and a house said to have been theirs still stands there.

Today it is part of the Indian holding company Eurasia Group and makes specialty teas for international sale.
